who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
task: Prove a property of sans-IO Rust that used to need a simulation test: a pure function, a state machine's step, or what survives a crash on the disk world
do: 1. State it in Rust, beside the code, as `#[blaze::theorem] fn name(args) -> bool`: early `return true` for inputs outside the property's domain (for the disk: `!disk.wf() || !disk.small()`), then the property, built from small oracle functions (`kept`, `cut_to_a_prefix`) so each has a control test `the_oracle_catches_..`. A crash is quantified by its witness: take `cut: Vec<Kept>`, return true when `!disk.allows(&cut)`, then `disk.crash(&cut)` (crates/blaze-core/src/world/disk.rs has three worked theorems). Put `/// The invariant: ..` on it. 2. Run it before proving it: a `blaze_sim::check` test that draws inputs and requires the theorem function true, with `must_reach` points so it is not vacuous (disk.rs, `the_theorems_hold_where_they_are_run`). 3. Get the models: `blaze prove -p <crate> --emit <dir>` (or, in blaze's tree, a golden test like hir-ty-lean's `blaze_cores_world_models_are_its_sources`); a `refused` line names the construct the translator does not take yet (`blaze prove --subset` counts them). 4. Prove `<name>.spec.proof : <name>.spec.statement` in `crates/<crate>/lean/<Crate>/<Module>.lean`. Try `blaze_auto [defs]` first. For loops: one specification per loop, an equation `loop fuel .. = Result.ok r` with `r` characterized by plain list facts, proved by induction on `fuel`; then the function's; one constant fuel for the whole theorem (2^67: a slice is at most 2^64 - 1 long and a nested call gets its caller's remaining fuel). State what stays the same about a collection by key, not by position. For the disk, import and use `BlazeCore.World.{DiskAllows, DiskMap, DiskBytes, DiskCrash}` (allows_orders, the sorted map, one file's bytes, take/put/flush/sync/crash) rather than unfolding the world again. 5. Check: `blaze prove -p <crate>` says `proved` with the three axioms; in blaze's tree also add the theorem to lean/theorems.json, write `(proved: <file>)` on the statement, and run `uv run --frozen python harness/v2/lean_gate.py '{"command": "write"}'` then `'{"command": "sources"}'`. Division of work that held on 2026-11-14: the main agent writes the statements and the lemma statements exactly; an Opus lane per proof file proves them, building with leanvm.sh in its own VM lane; the main agent rebuilds every library and runs `#print axioms` before committing. Tell the lane to STOP and report if a statement looks false.
why: On 2026-11-14 this took the disk world from nothing to three proved crash theorems in a night: the loop specifications (500 to 1,200 lines a file) were each done by an Opus lane in 9 to 21 minutes from exact statements, and a lane found one theorem false as stated before writing a line (no bound on a file's barriers; a model's `Vec::push` fails at usize::MAX elements), which 4,000 runs of the same theorem function had not. What cost time was never the proving: it was statements without their bounds, and tools run on the wrong tree.
